title: API Client HTTPS over the shared SocketProvider carrier boundary
summary: API Client keeps HTTP/TLS authority while Socket Intention dynamically selects a raw SocketProvider stream for each request; optional post-selection admission can require exact lower-route evidence.
invariants: ApiHttpsTransport owns HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, redirects, TLS identity, SNI and ALPN.
SocketProvider owns native carrier acquisition and retains the exact selected SocketAddress object.
ApiSocketProviderConnector does not choose TCP, XTP, Unix or any other socket family.
ApiSocketIntentionRouteResolver performs fresh negotiation on every resolve and does not cache a startup route.
API Client route requirements remain exact ooRexx objects in negotiation metadata; they are not converted into socket-family policy.
Lower carrier negotiation requires a stream but not a secure socket because API Client TLS runs above it; TLS SocketProvider is excluded from the default raw carrier schemes.
An optional ApiSocketRouteAdmissionPolicy runs after selection and before SocketProvider acquisition and receives the exact selected address/request/selection objects.
ApiSocketRequiredMetadataPolicy compares deployment-required address evidence exactly and fails closed on missing or mismatched evidence.
The adapter assigns no XTP, LDAP, private-CA or attestation semantics to metadata; those meanings and evidence are owned below this boundary.
No caller request boolean is itself accepted as authenticated route evidence.
The adapter creates an architectural HTTPS-over-XTP route but does not constitute live HTTPS-over-XTP qualification.

provenance.claim: Optional ApiSocketConnector acquisition while retaining ApiRxSockConnector as default.
dev3 adds fresh Socket Intention selection plus optional exact selected-route admission before SocketProvider acquisition.
Provider owns streamSenderAt and exact SocketAddress acquisition.
Current XTP context provides per-service protection with LDAP Identity Directory and Secret Broker key-source paths.
Authenticated remote-route admission is a separate platform authority and must bind attestation to the actual peer/channel, not caller options.

open: Run carrier, dynamic resolver and route-admission deterministic suites under ooRexx 5.3.0 r13196 from the current candidate.
Bind a real lower security/route authority to selected SocketAddress evidence; do not manufacture evidence in API Client.
Qualify an exact XTP dev34 selected sender/stream with bounded provider-native readiness.
Run live private-CA API Client HTTPS over that XTP carrier before making an HTTPS-over-XTP production claim.
